    Arm level data to pairwise contrasts

    Source: R/meta-network.R
    meta_pairwise.Rd

    meta_pairwise() turns arm level data (one row per treatment arm) into contrast level data (one row per pair of arms within a study), computing the effect size of treat1 relative to treat2 with meta_effect_size(). Studies with more than two arms contribute every pairwise contrast, which is what meta_network() expects.

    Usage

    meta_pairwise(
  .data,
  study,
  treatment,
  measure = "OR",
  event = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  mean = NULL,
  sd = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  add = 0.5,
  to = c("only0", "all", "none")
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per study arm.

    study, treatment

    <data-masking> Columns identifying the study and the treatment of each arm.

    measure

    An effect size measure for two groups: "OR", "RR", "MD", "SMD" or "IRR".

    event, n, mean, sd, time

    <data-masking> Arm level summaries: events and sample sizes for "OR" and "RR"; means, standard deviations and sample sizes for "MD" and "SMD"; events and person time for "IRR".

    add, to

    Zero cell correction, see meta_effect_size().

    Value

    A <meta_es> with columns study, treat1, treat2, the arm summaries suffixed with 1 and 2, and .yi, .vi and .sei.

    Examples

    meta_pairwise(smoking_cessation, study = study, treatment = trt,
  measure = "OR", event = xi, n = ni)
#> # A meta_es: 28 rows x 10 columns
